All processing happens on this device and never uses the network.

Used for JPEG and HEIF. If you choose “Same as Source” and a photo exports as one of those formats, this quality setting is used. 16-bit and wide-gamut sources such as Display P3 are written as 8-bit sRGB.
When this is on, exported files use a random name instead of the original. This helps keep dates out of names like IMGXXXX-XX-XX.
The watermark width is a percentage of the photo’s shorter side, and the original aspect ratio is kept.

When this is on, exported files have all metadata from the original removed, including: Camera settings (camera, lens, shutter, aperture, ISO, focal length, and other EXIF data) Date and time taken, and location (GPS) Captions, keywords, copyright, and other IPTC / XMP fields Manufacturer private data (MakerNote) Embedded thumbnails and other auxiliary metadata Camera-specific ICC color profiles (output is standardized to sRGB)
When this is off, those shooting details are kept as much as possible. The orientation tag is rewritten to “up” because the pixels are already rotated upright. The original embedded thumbnail is still omitted so an unwatermarked preview is not carried over. 16-bit and wide-gamut sources such as Display P3 are written as 8-bit sRGB.
